messages:
oliver: Procurement looped me on FiscalAI vs RecurScan proposals. pricing units aren't aligned; need quick hygiene check before i reply.
sana: share the snippets? curious if either charges for reconciliation deltas.
oliver: pasted vendor excerpts below: 
```
FiscalAI (Enterprise): $0.045 per invoice processed; line-item extraction included up to 12 lines/invoice, $0.0015 per extra line. Reconciliation events billed $0.02/event (unmatched line, credit note, reversal). Attachments $0.007/page unless ingested via S3 (waived). Min annual commit: $50k. Includes SSO and API. Onboarding: 30h included.
RecurScan (Enterprise): $0.055 per invoice or $0.04 at >150k/mo commitment. Alternative meter: $0.035 + $0.002 per extracted field for complex invoices. PDFs $0.01/page. Min commit: $35k. PS scoping billed separately.
```
meera: That reconciliation-event fee on FiscalAI is new; could be expensive during onboarding. RecurScan's hybrid also risky.
finance-ops: Reminder of our hard requirements: 1) reconciled payload must include GL mapping, tax/discount lines, FX adjustments, and a delta flag; 2) programmatic export: nightly S3 dump + realtime webhook; 3) audit log (per event) retained 7 years and exportable to our SIEM; 4) must support KMS/HSM and sign our DPA; 5) processing SLAs: nightly <3h, urgent <30m.
oliver: Procurement specifically asked me to confirm: how each vendor counts line-items/fields/events, sample cost at our projected 1.35M invoices/yr (including worst-case line counts), whether rule exports are supported, and whether they will accept acceptance-test benchmarks + remedies.
sana: Add to the email: ask whether reconciliation events are charged only for post-acceptance unmatched rate or also for tentative unmatched during processing. We need clarity.
meera: Also request: 1) a sample mapped JSON payload for one of our typical vendor invoices (we'll redact), 2) a line-count distribution CSV so we can model per-line costs, 3) sample SLA and credits language, and 4) whether GL mapping rules can be exported as YAML/JSON and version-controlled.
procurement-bot: Reminder: attach RFP + sample BigQuery export and use /procure/reply-template-v7. Include cost model template.
oliver: Draft vendor questions i'm about to send  please review: 
- Can you ingest our BigQuery export + GCS attachments? Any schema gaps?
- Provide precise pricing formula: how you count invoices vs pages vs extracted fields vs reconciliation events. Include worked examples.
- Provide a cost model spreadsheet for our projected volumes (50k/150k/300k monthly bands and 1.35M/yr) with best/worst-case line counts.
- Do you include full line-item extraction (tax/discounts/FX) in the per-invoice price or bill separately? If separate, list per-line/item fees.
- How are "reconciliation events" defined and billed? Are interim unmatched states billed? Can we exclude onboarding noise?
- Is SSO (SAML + SCIM) included? Is SCIM provisioning supported?
- Can GL mappings and reconciliation rules be exported as YAML/JSON and stored in our repo? Is there versioning/rollback?
- What onboarding PS hours are included vs billable? Can you commit X hours in year 1 as part of the package?
- SLA language for processing latency and accuracy targets; what credits/remedies do you provide for missed SLAs or acceptance failures?
- Will you sign our DPA and accept KMS/HSM key control requirements? List subprocessors.
- Can you provide programmatic export (S3 dump + webhooks) and audit logs formatted for Splunk ingestion? Retention guarantees?
- Do you offer a 30-day right-to-exit in year 1 if accuracy benchmarks during sandbox acceptance are not met?

sana: I'd add: request sample invoice PDF + mapped JSON back for one of our redacted vendors so we can sanity-check mapping quality. Also ask for an example contract clause that limits monthly charges (cap) to a negotiated effective per-invoice rate to avoid runaway costs.
meera: Negotiation levers to prepare: tiered per-invoice thresholds with steep discounts at 100k+/mo, waive reconciliation-event fees for first 90 days or until acceptance, include 40-80h PS in year 1, cap effective per-invoice rate (e.g., no more than $0.05 effective), and credits schedule tied to acceptance accuracy.
finance-ops: Hard stop items: must export mapping rules and provide SIEM-ready audit logs. If vendor refuses either, move to next. Also push for explicit subcontractor disclosure in the contract.
noliver: I'll send this consolidated list to both vendors in one thread and paste responses here. If anyone wants to tweak wording before i send, ping now. Thanks :white_check_mark:
